drafting_notes:
AUDIENCE: Year 2-3 (ages 7-9).
THE LADDER measures how long the wait is: immediately (no wait at all) < soon (short wait) < later (a real wait) < eventually (long slow process) < someday (unknown far future). Every frame must stage HOW LONG the wait is with a physical or calendar fact: 'the kettle is already whistling' (no wait), 'before the ice cream melts' (short), 'once the shopping is done' (a real wait), 'brick by brick over many months' (long process), 'when I am grown up' (far future dream).
SECOND-FIT TRAPS: soon vs later (give soon a visible countdown already running; give later an unhurried same-day wait); eventually vs someday (eventually ends an ONGOING process already in motion; someday is a wish with no process started); immediately vs soon (immediately is a zero-gap response, mid-emergency or mid-command).
TENSE LAW: at least two candidates must survive grammar in every frame; the wait-length fact picks the answer.
SLOTS: clause-final ('We can leave ___') or sentence-initial with a comma work for all five.
SURFACES: adverbs; the surface form of every candidate is the word itself, unchanged, in every frame.

contrasts.line: immediately has no wait at all; soon has a short wait already starting.
immediately is this instant; later is after a real wait.
immediately happens at once; eventually comes after slow progress.
immediately is for right now; someday is for a far-off wish.
soon has a brief wait; immediately has none.
soon is close, like a countdown; later is an unhurried wait.
soon is a short wait; eventually follows a slow build-up.
soon is coming shortly; someday is an unknown far-off wish.
later waits a while; immediately happens at once.
later is an unhurried wait; soon is just a brief wait.
later can be after chores today; eventually needs slow progress.
later is a real wait you can plan; someday is far and uncertain.
eventually ends a slow process; immediately has no wait.
eventually comes after steady progress; soon is only a short wait.
eventually follows a slow build-up; later is just after a while.
eventually has progress already going; someday is only a far-off wish.
someday is a far-off wish; immediately is right now.
someday is unknown and far away; soon is shortly.
someday is a far-off dream; later is a wait you can plan.
someday has no process started; eventually finishes one.
